title: inFact: Organic Food Myths
summary: Skeptic show arguing organic farms still use pesticides, reject efficient modern inputs, and deliver no real health or taste difference: organic is marketing.

organic is about marketing not about science not about health

you have to dig past a much larger number of studies that find no difference at all
organic practices however prohibit both of these Innovations

verdicts.note: Organic standards ban synthetic fertilizers and genetically engineered varieties, but conventionally bred modern varieties are allowed.
Supports the fertiliser half: mineral N fertilisers are barred under organic standards; says nothing about crop varieties.

The rules bar synthetic fertilizers not on the National List (205.203(e)) and genetically engineered varieties (205.105(e)), but they allow untreated conventional seed of any variety when no organic equivalent is available (205.204(a)), so modern conventionally bred varieties are not barred.

Organic is defined as using no synthetic inputs, but the comparisons Ponisio reviews often use modern varieties on organic plots; the problem is few varieties bred for organic conditions, not a rule barring modern varieties.
